func_8003D468_3E068.title: Initialize or reset the scenario interpreter
func_8003D468_3E068.summary: Prepares the native scenario VM, resetting shared interpreter and dialog configuration.
behavior: The native scenario interpreter executes 32-bit instructions and follows pointers to 16-bit glyph/control streams. This initializer resets the VM input/configuration state and selects its scenario/resource context.

Calling with a null script and file_id -1 clears the program counter and resource context. It does not allocate a message window. The initializer also clears transient native flag 0x82; callers preserving an existing flag state must restore that state when their own interaction ends.

A private dialog must first verify that the scenario manager exists and no scenario or message window currently owns the shared interpreter. Reset the interpreter before allocating and configuring a new window, then publish a persistent instruction stream only after allocation succeeds.

The no-file reset selects controller source 3 (merged controllers), character -1, window slot 0 with origin (24,24), style 0 and animation 0, and typing mode 1. It does not free existing windows; callers must finish ownership-aware window cleanup separately.
cautions: This function mutates shared scenario state; it must not reset a conversation or replacement scenario owned by another native task.
A successful reset does not prove that a window was allocated or that the world is safe for interactive UI.
Keep instruction arrays, text streams and callback targets alive until the interpreter and closing animation finish.

Native callers may establish player control locks before calling this initializer. An entry hook cannot assume those bits still belong to the previous interaction; do not clear replacement locks during cleanup.
func_8003D468_3E068.exampleExplanation: Complete C syntax using the reviewed 32-bit native interface. The engine owns these globals and resources; respect the stated lifecycle and ownership checks.

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: Scenario instruction stream, or null for the established reset operation.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: Scenario resource context; -1 is the established no-file/reset value.

func_8003D468_3E068.returns: Returns 0 when the scenario-manager pointer is null; otherwise returns 1 after resetting or starting the scenario.

func_8000C260_CE60.title: Allocate and configure a native message window
func_8000C260_CE60.summary: Allocates one message-window slot and configures its position, style and animation.
func_8000C260_CE60.declaration: extern void func_8000C260_CE60(int slot, int x, int y, int target_x, int target_y, int style, int animation);
behavior: Creates a 0x1818-byte native window allocation and stores its pointer in the selected entry of D_80167C48_168848. The three established slots are 0 through 2.
Style definitions come from the initialized table referenced by D_80167C54_168854. The ordinary US save sign uses slot 0, position and target (24,24), style 8 and animation 0.
The function has no success return. Inspect the selected window pointer after the call. Native choice parsing assumes the window exists and can dereference null if allocation failed.
cautions: Do not publish a text/choice instruction stream before checking window allocation.
Do not overwrite an occupied slot or assume a style table is resident merely because the main executable is loaded.
func_8000C260_CE60.exampleExplanation: Complete C syntax using the reviewed 32-bit native interface. The engine owns these globals and resources; respect the stated lifecycle and ownership checks.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: Resident window-style table index. Style 8 is used by the ordinary save sign.

parameters.name: animation
parameters.description: Native animation/configuration argument. The established stationary dialog call uses 0.

func_8000C260_CE60.returns: No return value; a nonnull selected slot is the allocation-success check.

func_8000C878_D478.title: Release a native message window
func_8000C878_D478.summary: Releases the native allocation belonging to a message-window slot.
behavior: Releases the selected native window and clears its slot in D_80167C48_168848.
Use a validated slot and verify that its current pointer still belongs to the interaction being closed. A room change or replacement scenario can transfer shared dialog ownership.
This is window cleanup, not a complete scenario cancellation API. Interpreter state, pending callbacks and acquired player-control bits require their own ownership-aware completion.
cautions: Do not release a replacement scenario window simply because it occupies the same numeric slot.

func_8003E6C0_3F2C0.title: Parse the native scenario choice list
func_8003E6C0_3F2C0.summary: Converts scenario choice instructions into selectable native dialog records.
behavior: Invoked by scenario opcode 0x8011. The following instruction stream contains four-word records of text opcode 0x8010, label pointer, branch opcode 0x800A and branch pointer, terminated by opcode 0x8012.
Constructs five-word (20-byte) runtime records in D_801C7808_1C8408 and stores the selected-record pointer in D_801C7800_1C8400. The usual Yes/No order places Yes first and No second.

Returns a pointer to the 0x8012 instruction that terminates the definitions. A return hook is the boundary after the runtime records exist; selection changes made before parsing completes are overwritten by the parser.
cautions: The parser expects the scenario window to be allocated. Window allocation failure must be handled before publishing a choice script.
Only change the selection when the current interpreter and choice records still belong to the intended scenario.
Runtime storage has capacity for 10 choice records. The native parse loop does not enforce that bound; validate custom instruction streams before publishing them.

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: First four-word text/branch choice definition, with a 0x8012 terminator after the last record.

func_8003E6C0_3F2C0.returns: Pointer to the 0x8012 sentinel in the scenario instruction stream.

D_80077858_78458.title: Native scenario instruction pointer
D_80077858_78458.summary: Pointer to the next instruction in the shared native scenario VM.
behavior: A null pointer indicates no current instruction stream. The native VM advances this pointer through 32-bit instructions and follows text, callback and branch operands.
Text operands address 16-bit glyph/control streams, not C strings. The US font maps printable ASCII 0x20 through 0x7E to glyph indices 0 through 94 by subtracting 0x20.

Publishing a custom stream transfers execution to shared native interpreter state. Allocate its window first, hold every referenced array/callback for the full lifetime, and detect replacement ownership before cancellation or cleanup.
cautions: This is a pointer variable, not instruction storage or a byte offset.
Network or user text must be converted to bounded native glyphs. Never reinterpret arbitrary text bytes as 16-bit controls or 32-bit instructions.

D_80077860_78460.title: Native scenario manager task pointer
D_80077860_78460.summary: Pointer to the native task that owns the shared scenario interpreter.
behavior: A live scenario manager is a prerequisite for opening an ordinary native dialog.
Remember the manager identity while an interaction is active. If the manager pointer changes, the old interaction must treat shared scenario/window ownership as replaced.
cautions: A nonnull manager alone does not establish that its interpreter and windows are idle or that the world is safe for input.

D_80167C48_168848.title: Native message-window slots
D_80167C48_168848.summary: Three pointers to native message-window allocations.
behavior: Each array entry is a window pointer. The allocator stores its result here; cleanup clears the selected slot.
Check all three slots before claiming an idle shared dialog interface. Slot zero is used by the ordinary save-sign dialog.
The signed 16-bit animation state is at window +0x30. Opening uses states 1 through 3; closing uses states 5 and 6. A ready window and an absent window must be distinguished by checking the pointer.

Each window contains 120 native glyph records of 0x30 bytes, starting at window +0x198. The native allocator searches these records; bound a custom prompt and its labels to the available glyph capacity.
cautions: The array contains pointers, not three contiguous 0x1818-byte windows.
Do not dereference a freed slot or consider a null pointer a successfully opened window.

D_80167C54_168854.title: Native message-window style table pointer
D_80167C54_168854.summary: Pointer to the initialized native message-window style definitions.
behavior: Generic native setup initializes the table; opening a save sign first is not a prerequisite.
The US table at runtime 0x800627F0 uses records of 0x24 bytes. Style 8 supplies the ordinary save-sign background and palette with width 256 pixels and a height of nine 8-pixel strips, or 72 pixels.
cautions: The symbol stores a table pointer; it is not the first style record itself.
Keep native setup/teardown and style-index validity separate from window allocation success.

D_801C7774_1C8374.title: Scenario typing-cancel continuation address
D_801C7774_1C8374.summary: Native 32-bit continuation address used by B while typing or waiting for text.
behavior: Stores an instruction-stream address, not a choice index or Boolean result. During native typing/text-wait handling, B branches to a nonzero address in this field; zero invokes the general native cancel path.
The choice-list B path is separate: it resumes four words after the 0x8012 choice terminator. Provide an explicit safe branch at that continuation when creating a custom Yes/No script.
Keep the continuation inside a persistent instruction stream owned by the current scenario.
cautions: Do not infer that all native cancel paths use this field; the choice B path has its own continuation rule.

D_801C7800_1C8400.title: Selected native choice-record address
D_801C7800_1C8400.summary: Native 32-bit address of the currently selected scenario choice record.
behavior: Points into the five-word runtime choice-record table after the choice parser completes.

A two-choice Yes/No list uses the first record for Yes and the next record, five words later, for No. A private dialog can choose No initially after parsing to avoid accepting a held confirmation input.
cautions: The stored value is a native address, not 0 for Yes or 1 for No.
Do not select a record outside the parsed list or modify a replacement native conversation.

D_801C7808_1C8408.title: Native parsed choice-record storage
D_801C7808_1C8408.summary: Shared native storage for five-word scenario choice records.
behavior: The choice parser converts each four-word script record into a five-word, 20-byte runtime record.
Selection points at a runtime record, while the branch continuation refers back to the scenario instruction stream. These are distinct layouts and addresses.
Native runtime storage holds at most 10 records. The parser does not bounds-check its input list, so custom scripts must not exceed this capacity.
cautions: Do not append records past the 10-record native capacity or treat the unsized extern as a dynamically growing array.

D_801C7900_1C8500.title: Scenario controller-input source
D_801C7900_1C8500.summary: Native integer selecting controller-one, controller-two or merged scenario input.
behavior: The scenario input sampler interprets 1 as controller one, 2 as controller two and 3 as merged input from both. This is an enumerated selector, not a general bitmask.
Zero and other values leave the previously sampled scenario input unchanged. Do not write zero expecting it to clear or disable input.
The scenario initializer selects source 3. Set source 1 after initialization when only controller one should respond.
cautions: Controller-input ownership is distinct from the player movement/control mask at D_800C7AE0.

D_800C7DB0_C89B0.title: Derived gameplay-controller records
D_800C7DB0_C89B0.summary: Inline storage for four derived gameplay-controller records, separate from raw dialog input.
behavior: Inline native storage at full-system +0x3B0F0 contains four records of 0x18 bytes each. It is distinct from the raw controller input used by the scenario sampler.

The native gameplay-input copier fills these records from raw input only while both D_800C7AE2 and D_800C7AE3 are zero. Otherwise it decays the stick state and recomputes analog quantities without copying new buttons.

The scenario sampler reads raw controller input separately. Filtering the derived gameplay records after the native input-copy update can suppress player buttons/stick while leaving the native dialog responsive; it does not require changing raw input or holding a global player lock between updates.
cautions: This symbol is inline storage, not a pointer variable.
Player-input and native scenario-input storage are separate. Clearing raw input would also make an interactive dialog unresponsive.
Acquire and release the associated control lock according to scenario ownership. Do not clear a lock installed by a replacement native scene.
D_800C7DB0_C89B0.exampleExplanation: The example validates the record index and reads its native held-button halfword. It does not modify raw input or player-control ownership.

func_80004AF8_56F8.title: Update derived gameplay-controller input
func_80004AF8_56F8.summary: Copies or decays native controller state into the derived gameplay input records.
behavior: Updates the four 0x18-byte derived gameplay-controller records at D_800C7DB0_C89B0 from the native raw input records while both D_800C7AE2 and D_800C7AE3 are zero.

When either lock byte is nonzero, the function decays stick state and recomputes analog quantities without copying new buttons. Previously held/pressed values require explicit consideration; setting a lock is not equivalent to clearing the derived input.

A return hook observes or filters the completed derived sample. The scenario input sampler reads separate raw controller storage, so clearing derived gameplay buttons/stick at this boundary can leave native dialog input responsive.
Reads the native OS controller messages and updates raw input before completing the derived gameplay sample. Its return is a useful observation boundary after controller processing.
cautions: Do not overwrite raw controller storage when the native scenario still needs to receive input.
If filtering a derived record, preserve its connected-status halfword and respect scenario/room ownership.
Calling this routine directly can block while waiting for an SI/controller message. Observe its normal native invocation instead of adding extra calls.
func_80004AF8_56F8.exampleExplanation: The native return hook reads controller-one held buttons after the derived input update. It does not modify raw input or introduce global control ownership.
